audits.subsystem: Portfolio, capital accounting, fees, and per-market/batch statistics (src/trading/Portfolio.ts, capital.ts, fees.ts, src/backtest/stats/*)
valuableKnowledge: `round2` in TS rounds to 8 dp, not 2 (src/trading/utils/rounding.ts:10-12: `Math.round(n * 1e8) / 1e8`). Positions, cost basis and realizedPnl keep 8 dp, so a Rust port must not add 2 dp rounding to match the name. Only the final MarketStats fields are rounded to 2 or 4 dp (marketStats.ts:186-198).

Cash reservation is separate from the strategy-facing order record (Portfolio.ts:122-127, 210-297). A BUY's obligation is released only by an authoritative final quantity: rejection or kill gives 0, 'filled' gives the full size, or a done/WS update that carries sizeMatched. A plain REST cancel ack keeps the hold (Portfolio.ts:276-277).

Trade-status WS updates (MATCHED/MINED/CONFIRMED/RETRYING/FAILED) carry a single trade's size, not cumulative size_matched, so they must never set an order's final filled quantity for cash (Portfolio.ts:228-230).

Client-id reuse guard (Portfolio.ts:189-197, 307-312): a late event carrying an older exchange orderId must not touch a newer submission with the same clientOrderId, and must not merge two cash obligations. capital.test.ts:331 and :366 cover this.

A fill can arrive before the order's exchange id is known. It is buffered by orderId (pendingFilledByOrderId, Portfolio.ts:849-858; unlinkedCashFills, :292-296) and applied on accept/open (:644, :678). Fills are de-duplicated by id, with splits and merges under the `split:` and `merge:` key prefixes (Portfolio.ts:554, :781, :796).

A non-post-only BUY reserves `price*size + taker fee` at the hardcoded 700 bps even if it will rest as a maker. Post-only reserves no fee, and SELLs reserve nothing (capital.ts:16-28). Confirmed sale proceeds can be reused immediately, so turnover may exceed capital (capital.test.ts:395).

OrderManager adds obligations it has emitted but the Portfolio has not applied yet (unapplied submissions, splits and merges) to the decision snapshot (OrderManager.ts:120-140). Pending merges reduce mergeable qty (OrderManager.ts:412-420). This matters for cascading account callbacks inside a tick.

The funding rejection reason is a parsed string contract: `insufficient_capital(required=X,available=Y)` (OrderManager.ts:151-155), regex-parsed by the simulator trace (simulator/contracts.ts:186-197).

Capital is a per-market allowance, not a wallet balance (Strategy.ts:337-345). StrategyRunner keeps one Portfolio per market and sends old-market events to the old portfolio, so they never fund the new allowance (StrategyRunner.ts:290-309, 600-607; capital.test.ts:531, :545).

Taker fees are charged in USDC on both sides. BUY fees are added to cost basis (and avgEntryPrice), SELL fees reduce realized proceeds (Portfolio.ts:894-941). MarketStats.feesPaid only reports fees and must not subtract them again (Portfolio.test.ts:118-172).

tradeCount counts fill records, not orders. A taker sweep makes one Fill per book level (BacktestExecution.ts:146-170), and each fill's fee is rounded separately to 4 dp with a 0.0001 floor (fees.ts:18-24). For parity, Rust must split fills per level and round fees per fill the same way.

Zero-activity rows keep the denominator stable. When nothing was held or traded, runSingleMarket still emits MarketStats with skipReason 'no_in_window_activity' and output skipReason 'no_activity' (runSingleMarket.ts:539-566). It returns marketStats=null only when no tick was seen at all (:517-527). The two cases are counted differently by aggregateProcessor.ts:104-118.

MarketStats.intentMeta keeps the first fill's order meta per clientOrderId, taken from `ordersByClientId[cid].meta` at harvest time (runSingleMarket.ts:325-328, marketStats.ts:171-180). Fills without a clientOrderId always count. export-trade-features reads intentMeta[0] (export-trade-features.ts:230).

Batch streaks are order-sensitive. Segments sort markets by slug epoch before reducing (backtestSegments.ts:172), and the extension path re-sorts the union chronologically before recomputing (db/backtests.ts:1036-1045).

qualitySystem/qualityTrade use population mean/std and return null when std is 0 or |q| > 99,999,999. The guard exists because a float-residue std overflowed the DECIMAL(14,6) column (batchStats.ts:162-175).
durationWallClockMs is the union of per-market [startedAtMs, finishedAtMs] intervals, so idle gaps between an original run and a later --extend are excluded (batchStats.ts:286-295, wallClock.ts).
designDebt: CONFIRMED PnL BUG: merges inside a market lose their proceeds from MarketStats.pnl. positions_merged credits cash (Portfolio.ts:562) but realizes nothing. A partial merge keeps the full cost basis (:576), a full merge deletes it (:577), and computeMarketStats never sees merges (marketStats.ts:163-169). A scratch run gave buy 10U@0.4 + 10D@0.5, merge 10 → pnl 0 (true +1); merge 5 → pnl -4 (true +1); split 10 + merge 10 → pnl -10 (true 0). This affects buyBothSidesAndMerge.v1, engine-exerciser, and any protocol strategy that merges.

The simulator trace already uses cash-based PnL (`pnlIfUp = cashDelta + up.qty`, simulator/contracts.ts:180-181). So the trace UI and the persisted MarketStats.pnl disagree for merge strategies. The Rust design should compute pnl as cash_end - starting + settlement value, and assert it equals the cost-basis decomposition.

Rust WIP bug: with the realistic flag split_zero_cost_basis=false, split cost is put into position cost basis (portfolio.rs:549-560). compute_market_stats then subtracts split_cost again (stats.rs:241-246), so split cost is counted twice in the realistic profile.

SELLs are never checked against inventory, in OrderManager or BacktestExecution (only merges check positions, BacktestExecution.ts:310-312). An oversell fills, cash is credited in full (capital.ts:39), but realized PnL only counts min(size, qty) (Portfolio.ts:925). Cash and PnL then diverge, and the backtest allows something the exchange would reject.

The fee is recomputed from feeRateBps in four places: capital.ts:31-38, Portfolio.ts:894-899, marketStats.ts:128-134 and StrategyRunner.ts:612-623. The commitment uses hardcoded 700 bps (capital.ts:25), and the backtest always stamps 700 bps (BacktestExecution.ts:236). The Fill should carry a fee amount, as the Rust `Fill.fee` does, computed once from the per-market dated feeSchedule.

There are two unrelated 'capital' concepts. The per-market allowance (DEFAULT_STARTING_CAPITAL=500, capital.ts:6) actually gates orders. INITIAL_CAPITAL=1000 (cli/backtest.ts:737) only feeds capitalFinal = initial + sum(pnl), with no compounding (batchStats.ts:277).

The run-level computeBatchStats in aggregateProcessor.ts:168 runs in idx order, but insertBacktestRun persists only `capitalInitial` from it (db/backtests.ts:433). Every displayed metric comes from the time-sorted 'all' segment (dashboard batches.ts:271-277), so this call is vestigial.

BatchStatsFields docs disagree with the code. They say marketsSkipped is 'tradeCount === 0' and marketsPlayed is 'tradeCount > 0' (batchStats.ts:23-30). The code classifies by pnl sign (:194-235), so flat markets that did trade count as skipped and are left out of winRate.

`MarketStats.cost` is the remaining cost basis at settlement, not money spent. The directional-game dashboard uses `m.cost > 0` as its 'played' test (directional-game/route.ts:~70). So a buy-then-exit-before-close market, or split-only inventory (zero basis), counts as not played.

MarketStats.avgEntryPriceUp/Down is a fee-exclusive BUY VWAP that includes shares later sold (marketStats.ts:116-139). Position.avgEntryPrice is fee-inclusive average cost of what is left (Portfolio.ts:910-916). They are two different numbers with similar names.

positionMetrics (strategy-facing ctx.metrics.position) computes pnl_if_up_wins = up_shares - total_cost and ignores realizedPnl and split cost (positionMetrics.ts:44-46). This is a different PnL definition from MarketStats.

Fill harvest reads `portfolio.recentFills`, which is capped at 500 (Portfolio.ts:140), once after each tick, and drops fills without `market` (runSingleMarket.ts:322-331). Fills beyond 500 in one tick cascade, or fills missing market, change positions but are missing from tradeCount and fees.
mergeValue + redeemValue in computeMarketStats (marketStats.ts:141-157) just equals the winning side's share count. It adds complexity without changing the result.

Live-only reconciliation is mixed into the same class as backtest accounting: wsOpenOrders, pendingTradeStatus, 50k/10k bounded maps with 10% pruning. A JSON.stringify diff runs on every ws_order_update only to call a no-op logger (Portfolio.ts:479-480), there is dead logging code (Portfolio.ts:978-1013), and legacy costBasis typeof checks remain (:903-908).

There is no reversal path for a trade that goes MATCHED then FAILED. userWsAccountSource emits the fill once (emittedTradeIds) and Portfolio only moves on `fill` (Portfolio.ts:773-789). Positions and cash stay wrong when USER_WS_FILL_AT_STATUS=MATCHED.

The Rust WIP ports market resolution (stats.rs MarketResolution::from_telonex/from_gamma). The producer already resolves in TS (marketResolution.ts, telonexMarketResolution.ts) and ships it in MarketJobData, so Rust only needs to deserialize it. Porting it duplicates DB/Gamma-adjacent logic across the boundary.
outputContract: RunSingleMarketOutput JSON: {idx, slug, marketStats | null, eventsProcessed, eventsByType, durationMs, skipReason?: 'no_slug'|'no_resolution'|'unresolved_outcome'|'no_activity'|'incomplete_capture', coverageReasons?}. Consumed by src/backtest/aggregateProcessor.ts:92-118, which sorts by idx and turns null marketStats into a failure row via skipReason/coverageReasons, and by src/cli/backtest.ts (sequential path).

MarketStats JSON, camelCase, field for field: marketId, slug, finalOutcome ('UP'|'DOWN'), pnl (2 dp), tradeCount, tradeAsMaker, tradeAsTaker, feesPaid (2 dp), avgEntryPriceUp/Down (4 dp or null), upShares, downShares, mergableShares, cost, splitCost (2 dp), intentMeta (array, never null), skipReason? ('no_in_window_activity' only, a MySQL enum), recorderV4Capture?, execution? {machineId, workerChildId, startedAtMs, finishedAtMs, durationMs, eventsProcessed, eventsByType, commitSha}. Written column by column in src/db/backtests.ts:443-478 and 955-988 (schema src/db/schema.ts:183-240).
Minimum validation on persist: marketId string, slug string, finalOutcome UP/DOWN, pnl number (src/db/backtests.ts:186-197). Rows can be bare or {idx, stats}.

Batch aggregation (computeBatchStats, computeBacktestSegments) reads only MarketStats.pnl, feesPaid, tradeCount, tradeAsMaker, tradeAsTaker, skipReason, slug (for slugTs) and execution.{durationMs, startedAtMs, finishedAtMs} (batchStats.ts:180-343, backtestSegments.ts). It stays in TS and is also re-run from DB rows by src/cli/rebuild-backtest-segments.ts and applyExtensionToRun (db/backtests.ts:1036-1045).

Dashboard reads only MySQL rows: backtest_run_markets fields (dashboard/src/lib/queries/batches.ts:644-675), backtest_run_segments 'all' row for run summaries (batches.ts:271-277, 374-445), `cost`/`pnl` semantics in dashboard/src/app/api/directional-game/route.ts:~70, execution meta in leaderboard.ts. It imports only @polymarket-bot/stats/coverage and /wallClock, never portfolio code.

audits.subsystem: OrderManager + StrategyRunner + strategy SDK surface (src/trading/OrderManager.ts, StrategyRunner.ts, riskLimits.ts, cancellation.ts, capital.ts, runnerConfig.ts; src/strategy/Strategy.ts, StrategyContext.ts, strategyToolkit.ts, plugins/PluginSet.ts)
valuableKnowledge: Tick pipeline order is: OM.onMarketTick (due latency actions + simulated fills) → drain with strategy.onAccountEvent cascades → metrics → late-start gate → plugins.onMarketTick → strategy.onMarketTick → applyIntents → drain (StrategyRunner.ts:326-459). So fill callbacks on tick N see tick N's book (lastMarket is set at :313) but tick N-1's plugin snapshot (cachedPlugins is refreshed only at :437).

Cascades are breadth-first FIFO: events from a callback's intents go to the END of accountEventQueue (StrategyRunner.ts:551, :689). Sibling events already in the queue are processed before the strategy sees the results of its own new intents; the draining guard is at :569.

Every account event goes to strategy.onAccountEvent after Portfolio.apply + reconcile, including the bot's own synthesized order_submitted/order_accepted/order_open and every ws_order_update (StrategyRunner.ts:628-675). The number and order of callbacks therefore matter for parity.

Within one handleIntents call, all risk rejections are emitted before any executed event, whatever the intent order (OrderManager.ts:221-222, :247-248). The Rust WIP keeps this by pushing rejections to `out` first.

Risk counters are incremental within one intent list (riskLimits.ts:141-148, :208-215), but cancels never free capacity before confirmed events (riskLimits.ts:158-162; cancellation.test.ts:540). As a result, cancel-and-replace at the 100-order cap rejects the replacement.

Dedupe: placing a cid that is still active is silently dropped with no event (OrderManager.ts:466, :666). The cid is released on an immediate rejected/done result (:526-534, :739-747), on in-list cancel completion (:311-334), or in reconcile once Portfolio shows it closed and no unapplied submission with that cid exists (:161-174).

Unapplied submissions are tracked by OpenOrder object identity, not by cid (OrderManager.ts:108, :117, :164). This is what keeps a queued same-cid replacement deduped while the old order's order_done is drained (cancellation.test.ts:721-746, :923-958). The Rust WIP keys them by cid (native/crates/pmb-core/src/order_manager.rs:183, :665), which breaks this; it needs a per-submission generation id.

Pending capital: withPendingCapital adds unapplied BUY commitments and unapplied split costs to reservedCash, both in the strategy's decision portfolio and in funding checks (OrderManager.ts:121-140, :151-155). It is therefore sequential within a list and visible to earlier queued callbacks (capital.test.ts:190-212, :459-476).

Merge size is clamped to held positions minus unapplied merges, so two merges in one list cannot spend the same pairs twice (OrderManager.ts:412-431). size<=0 returns [] silently (:411), while invalid asset ids return merge_failed (:399-410).

placementRejections drops risk rejections for a cid that is currently active (OrderManager.ts:176-184), because Portfolio's order_rejected deletes the open order by cid (Portfolio.ts:682-690). Without it, a blocked duplicate would kill tracking of the live order (cancellation.test.ts:748-766).

trackReferences: when a list contains any cancel, a local copy of open/history refs is updated after each intent (OrderManager.ts:268-337). This makes 'place, then cancel the acknowledged exchange id' and 'cancel, then re-place the same cid' work inside one list (cancellation.test.ts:362).

Cancels are resolved differently by kind. cancel_batch/cancel_market are resolved before dispatch (unknown_client_order, conflicting refs, missing_exchange_order_id unless dry-run, terminal orders skipped, dedupe by exchange id, at most 3000; cancellation.ts:61-127). A non-dry-run cancel_order goes straight to the adapter (OrderManager.ts:561), and backtest binds it to the current sim order by cid (BacktestExecution.ts:680-686).

Market rotation (live multi-market runner): on the first tick of a new market, old open orders are cancelled with an immediate cancel_batch applied to the OLD portfolio with no strategy callbacks. Then beginMarket clears pending/dedupe, and a fresh strategy + pluginSet + Portfolio are created (StrategyRunner.ts:267-306).

Late events from an old market are routed to that market's portfolio and never reach the new strategy or its capital allowance (StrategyRunner.ts:598-608; capital.test.ts:531-596). Market lookup order is event.market → orderId map → assetId map → clientId map (set only on order_submitted) → current market (StrategyRunner.ts:692-720).

Synthetic feed ticks skip OM.onMarketTick entirely: no due latency actions, no GTD expiry, no maker fills (StrategyRunner.ts:326-334). In immediate mode the strategy can still take liquidity against the unchanged book, stamped with the clamped time (StrategyRunner.syntheticTicks.test.ts:94-176).

Plugins skip synthetic ticks unless they set handlesSyntheticTicks, but the snapshot is rebuilt on every tick (PluginSet.ts:72-79). Snapshot keys are plugin ids, undefined values are omitted, and a duplicate id is won by the last plugin (PluginSet.ts:90-101).

The plugin snapshot is tick-scoped: it is built once per tick and reused for every account callback until the next tick (StrategyRunner.ts:436-437, :655). Live feed values are captured when the tick ARRIVES, before the serial queue, via captureMarketTick (StrategyRunner.ts:249; ExternalFeedsRequestPlugin.ts:89-94).

PortfolioSnapshot.nowMs is NOT the tick time. It is set once by the first tick or event (initializeClock), advances only on account events as a monotone max, and the same frozen snapshot object is reused across ticks (Portfolio.ts:148-153, :434-437; StrategyRunner.clock.test.ts:200-250). basicFak builds its cids from it (basicFak.v1.ts:178).
Intents triggered by account events are stamped with lastMarket.timestamp, not the event time (StrategyRunner.ts:679). The same stamp feeds GTD validation and createdAtMs.

Live serial funnel: ticks, user-WS/poller events and WebUI commands run strictly one at a time, in arrival order. A thrown error rejects its own caller and is console.error'd, but never breaks the chain (StrategyRunner.ts:211-246; StrategyRunner.serial.test.ts:47-131).

Validation: price>0 and finite, size>0, assetId present, postOnly only on GTC/GTD, GTD needs a finite expireAtMs >= now+minGtdOffsetMs (60 s default), expireAtMs ignored for non-GTD (OrderManager.ts:756-780). The funding commitment for a BUY is price*size plus a 700 bps taker fee unless postOnly (capital.ts:16-28).

Batches dedupe, validate and fund each order separately and accept partial batches. A rejected order emits order_rejected with no prior order_submitted (OrderManager.ts:664-706), and Portfolio ignores it (Portfolio.ts:683-684).

Dry-run: place emits submitted+accepted+open with no orderId and never fills; cancels resolve locally (unknown exchange ids → cancel_failed); merge is simulated (OrderManager.ts:434-452, :508-521, :542-560). Split is NOT gated by OM (OrderManager.ts:386); live relies on a stub adapter for safety (trading-bot.ts:559-570).

Live placeLimit emits ONLY order_accepted; open/done/fills come later from the user WS (LiveExecution.ts:372-387). Backtest emits accepted, a MATCHED ws_order_update, fills and done synchronously, so strategies keyed on order_open/order_done see different sequences live and in backtest.

Backtest marks every accepted order MATCHED even with zero fills, and CONFIRMED immediately on a fill (BacktestExecution.ts:536-549, :589-600). So isOrderTradeStatusAtLeast(..., 'MATCHED'/'MINED') answers differently live and in backtest (strategyToolkit.ts:41-49; used by basicFak and buyBothSidesAndMerge).
isWarmed returns true when warmup is absent or in status 'error'; it blocks only on 'warming' (strategyToolkit.ts:51-56).

Window start: strategies call parseGammaMarketStartMs (eventStartTime, else startDate). The backtest derives eventStartTime from the slug because Gamma startDate is the creation time, about 22h earlier (strategyToolkit.ts:16-27; cli/backtest.ts:190-195). The live late-start skip uses the same function (StrategyRunner.ts:380).

The drain budget is per drain call: default 4200, env MAX_EVENTS_PER_DRAIN, validated as a positive safe integer (runnerConfig.ts:1-10). Tests require a 42-order FOK fill burst to fit, and a low budget to drop identically in live and backtest configs (runnerConfig.test.ts:111-145).
designDebt: Queued intent mode is dead in production: runSingleMarket uses 'immediate' (runSingleMarket.ts:203), the trading-bot defaults to it (trading-bot.ts:172), and latency lives in BacktestExecution. Do not port pendingIntents (OrderManager.ts:157-158, :201-205, :229-249) beyond, at most, a ts-compat flag.

When maxEventsPerDrain is exceeded, the runner silently clears the whole queue, fills and order_submitted included (StrategyRunner.ts:574-584). It logs only through the optional `log`, which is off in the default live config (trading-bot.ts:620-622). A dropped order_submitted leaves the cid permanently deduped and its cash reserved until the next market; Rust should treat this as a hard error or kill switch.

Risk limits ignore unapplied submissions from earlier lists in the same cascade, so orders placed from callbacks can exceed maxOpenOrders/maxAbsPosition, while funding does see pending orders (riskLimits.ts:47-54 vs OrderManager.ts:121-140).

The loss stop blocks every place_limit, including SELL exits, despite its 'allow exits' comment (riskLimits.ts:84-86, :165-170). With 500 USDC per-market capital and maxLossStop=500, it practically never fires.

There is no SELL inventory check and no share reservation for open SELLs: risk allows a projected short down to -2000 (riskLimits.ts:131-139), and Portfolio credits cash for a naked sell (capital.ts:30-40; Portfolio.ts:925-943).

OM validation has no tick-size check, no price<=1 or other bounds, no min size, no 15-order batch cap, and not Polymarket's GTD 'now+60s+lifetime' rule (OrderManager.ts:756-780). minGtdOffsetMs is documented as the '1-minute threshold' (:83-87).

Wall-clock fallbacks leak nondeterminism: `tick.snapshot.timestamp || Date.now()` (StrategyRunner.ts:314, :328, :457), `|| Date.now()` (:541, :679), the BACKTEST_WAIT_FOR_TECHNICAL_INDICATORS setTimeout polling loop (:404-434), and unseeded Math.random jitter (BacktestExecution.ts:240).

Live immediate mode awaits the REST place/cancel round trip inside the serial funnel (OrderManager.ts:523 under StrategyRunner.ts:211-246). That freezes the strategy and queues ticks during the round trip, while backtest models latency as asynchronous. This structural live/backtest mismatch should not be copied: make placement non-blocking with ack events.

cancel_order and cancel_batch treat in-flight orders differently. The batch path fails with missing_exchange_order_id (cancellation.ts:115-118), while a single cancel in backtest is queued and bound by cid (BacktestExecution.ts:680-686). Unknown targets silently no-op in backtest (:658-661) but produce cancel_failed live.

Dead code: the 'duplicate_clientOrderId' reason is never emitted anywhere (OrderManager.ts:312). SplitPositionsIntent.costPerShare is only logged (Strategy.ts:111; StrategyRunner.ts:526), yet the Rust WIP carries cost_per_share in ExecCommand::Split. The legacy Strategy.requiredFeeds seam is also unused (Strategy.ts:493-520).

The pending maps are keyed by object identity (OrderManager.ts:108-113), and Portfolio stores the event's `order` object and mutates it in place (Portfolio.ts:594-595, :620-623). Emitted events and older snapshots therefore alias live state; Rust needs explicit ids and must not reproduce the aliasing.
Position and orderbook metrics are recomputed for every tick and every account event (StrategyRunner.ts:337-351, :637-653), although only 4 strategies read ctx.metrics.
Live-only maps are never pruned: portfoliosByMarket and the three accountMarketBy* maps grow for as long as the process runs (StrategyRunner.ts:116-119).

An account event for the current market that arrives before the first tick goes into a temporary portfolio, which the first tick then overwrites in portfoliosByMarket (StrategyRunner.ts:599-604 vs :309), so the event is lost.

Rotation cancels only bot orders with a known exchange id: unacknowledged ones hit missing_exchange_order_id, and external wsOpenOrders are not touched (StrategyRunner.ts:274-289; cancellation.ts:115).

A synthetic tick's clamped timestamp can be ahead of the next real tick's exchange stamp, so OM nowMs and the stamps on callback intents can move backwards (syntheticTick.ts clamp vs base only; StrategyRunner.ts:313, :679).

LiveExecution ignores the postOrder response status (matched/unmatched/delayed), so terminal events for FOK orders depend entirely on the user WS (LiveExecution.ts:363-387). Until one arrives, the cid stays deduped and its capital reserved (OrderManager.ts:526-534).

Markets blocked by the late-start skip still run OM.onMarketTick and still deliver account callbacks to the strategy (the gate at StrategyRunner.ts:363-369 runs after :326-334; processAccountEvent has no gate).

Rust WIP status: order_manager.rs and rules.rs are not declared in pmb-core lib.rs (lib.rs:14-23), so they are not compiled. No runner exists, and strategy.rs Ctx has no Gamma market meta (eventStartTime/slug), no metrics, no balance, and only a boolean warmup.

It attaches ordersByClientId[cid].meta as intentMeta and also reads recentSplits (src/backtest/runSingleMarket.ts:309-340). recentFills is a 500-entry ring (Portfolio.ts:140).

The trace depends on engine processing order and TRACED_EVENT_KINDS.

valuableKnowledge: Post-only is checked against the book that is current when the (possibly delayed) order arrives, not at decision time. A crossing order is rejected whole with no partial fill, equality counts as crossing, and an empty opposing side accepts (BacktestExecution.ts:37-54; BacktestExecution.postOnly.test.ts:116-185).

A selected cancel binds to the acknowledged exchange orderId before latency is applied, so a delayed cancel cannot kill a replacement order that reuses the same clientOrderId (BacktestExecution.ts:680-682; docs/engine/backtest-execution.md:65).

cancel_market resolves its scope when it takes effect, so it includes orders that opened during the latency window. Delayed placements keep the market id from submission time even across a market rotation (BacktestExecution.ts:485-491, 744-751).

The pending queue is ordered by (executeAtMs, seq), and due actions run before GTD expiry and maker checks. On the same tick, GTD expiry wins over a maker fill (BacktestExecution.ts:779-816; test 211-250).

Fill ids are per submission (`${orderId}:${fillSeq}`, orderId `bt-${seq}-${cid}`), so reusing a clientOrderId never dedupes genuine fills. Portfolio dedupes only by fill.id (BacktestExecution.ts:92-96, 350; Portfolio.ts:781).

Live fill identity is shared by WS and REST: a taker fill's id is tradeId and a maker fill's id is `${tradeId}:${makerOrderId}`, so either source can arrive first without double-counting cash (userWsAccountSource.ts:312, 336; restPollAccountSource.ts:45-57; restPollCapital.test.ts:82-183).

On MAKER trades the top-level side/size/price belong to the taker. Our fills must come from maker_orders filtered by owner == our API key, because taker messages also carry other people's maker_orders (userWsAccountSource.ts:110-112, 283-326, 457).

A maker counterpart can sit on the opposite outcome token (mint/merge matching), so fills must use maker_orders[].asset_id/side/price rather than the trade's top-level asset. Current docs confirm that maker_orders carries side and fee_rate_bps (userWsAccountSource.ts:296-316).

Live cancel handling: only ids listed in `canceled` produce order_done. not_canceled, omitted ids, malformed responses and thrown errors produce non-terminal cancel_failed, and an already-terminal order gets no second terminal event (LiveExecution.ts:402-490).
Live placement emits only order_accepted (to link clientOrderId to orderId). The lifecycle comes from the user WS, which avoids duplicate transitions (LiveExecution.ts:373-386).

Batch results are checked entry by entry. A short or non-array response rejects the remaining orders, and a batch of more than 15 is rejected before signing, which matches the documented limit of 1-15 (LiveExecution.ts:166-178, 207-281).

The taker fee applies only to TAKER fills that carry an explicit feeRateBps. An explicit 0 is honored, the fee is deducted from SELL proceeds, and maker fills omit feeRateBps (restPollCapital.test.ts:115-127; BacktestExecution.ts:166-168).

Synthetic feed ticks must never run the simulator: re-testing resting orders against a stale book would create fills that live never gives (StrategyRunner.ts:315-326). The Rust trait already encodes this rule (execution.rs:66-67).
User-WS timestamps mix units: `timestamp` is in ms, while match_time/last_update are in seconds (userWsAccountSource.ts:66-83). Current user-channel docs confirm this.
Merge is clamped to min(requested, qtyA, qtyB), and OrderManager pre-clamps it to uncommitted positions. A split costs exactly 1 collateral per full set (BacktestExecution.ts:294, 310-313).

The recorded book never contains our own order. A BUY resting above the recorded best bid is therefore alone at its level (queue-ahead 0), and any ask at that price would hit it. worst_queue (BacktestExecution.ts:88-89) is too pessimistic there but too optimistic on size (full fill, line 102). A realistic model should set queue-ahead from the recorded size at our price when the order arrives.

The measured live distribution is placement 71-379 ms (avg 116) and cancel 65-210 ms (avg 91), measured from intent to portfolio visibility (MeasureLatency.md:18-19, 69-91). This is useful for fitting separate place and cancel latency distributions, but it is a round trip.

Order-channel mapping: CANCELLATION becomes order_done(canceled, filledSize=size_matched), size_matched >= original_size becomes order_done(filled), and anything else becomes order_open keyed by orderId only, which Portfolio reconciles (userWsAccountSource.ts:398-423).

designDebt: worst_queue fills the entire remaining size at once as soon as the opposite best trades through the price. There are no partials, no queue, and no cap by the volume that traded through (BacktestExecution.ts:88-107, 111-135).

Liquidity never depletes: taker fills walk ctx.lastMarket without changing it, so two orders in the same tick or latency window both consume the same levels (BacktestExecution.ts:139-190, 367-368, 523-524).

A crossing GTC takes the available depth and rests the remainder. The maker loop then fills that remainder at its own limit as a zero-fee MAKER fill, because the undepleted ask is still below the limit. With latency this happens on the same tick, with zero latency on the next (BacktestExecution.ts:447-469, 803-822).

Latency jitter uses unseeded Math.random, so runs are non-deterministic (BacktestExecution.ts:240). Place and cancel share one delay (195-197). Delayed actions run only on the next real book tick (StrategyRunner.ts:326), are stamped with that tick's time rather than executeAtMs, and see the post-event book (BacktestExecution.ts:765-801).

The fee is 700 bps for every market and date, rounded to 4 dp with a minimum of 0.0001 (fees.ts:10, 18-24; BacktestExecution.ts:236). The docs and changelog say: each market's own `feeSchedule` (since 2026-03-31), no fees on 15m crypto before 2026-01-05, 5m launched with fees on 2026-02-12, 5 dp rounding, minimum 0.00001, and a 20% crypto maker rebate (ignored here).

The TS minimum offset is 60 s (OrderManager.ts:189, 770) and the backtest expires orders at expireAtMs (BacktestExecution.ts:805), but the docs require expiration >= 3 min ahead and an effective expiry 60 s earlier. audits.reasoning:
Scope: about 2,700 lines of source plus about 1,080 lines of tests (3,790 total). The backtest simulator has only about 300 lines of real logic; the rest is event plumbing and code duplicated between the single-order and batch paths.

Backtest simulator: redesign it, but keep TS as the oracle. Its quirks are few, simple and easy to list: a full fill on trade-through, no liquidity depletion, a free maker fill of a crossing remainder, delayed actions run on the next book tick and stamped with that tick's time, unseeded jitter, and a fixed 700 bps fee at 4 dp. A small ts-compat setting for the FillModel, the LatencyModel and the fee can reproduce all of them, with jitter set to 0 for parity runs. That ts-compat run is what proves the port of the rest of the core (OrderManager, Portfolio, runner, strategies) through the trace diff (TRACE.md plus src/backtest/parity, which already exist in the WIP). Do not port the TS code structure. Build an event-time scheduler where actions fire at their exact time (the WIP trait's `advance_to` is the right hook), keep a simulated book that our own orders can deplete, and add queue-ahead plus seeded, separate place and cancel latency.

Two notes on the realistic profile. First, worst-queue is wrong in both directions: it is too pessimistic for orders that improve the spread and too optimistic on fill size. Second, the profile needs a source of per-market data that does not exist yet: capture the Gamma fields feeSchedule, feesEnabled, secondsDelay, tick size and min size at catalog time.

The Rust rules.rs needs fixes now. The taker delay is not "unverified": the official changelog gives 250 ms, then 50 ms from 2026-08-17, then 150 ms from 2026-09-04, and it should be keyed by trade time. GTD needs a 3-minute minimum lead and an effective expiry 60 s early.

Live: redesign from scratch against the V2 docs. There is no working oracle, because live has been broken since the 2026-04-28 V2 cutover. Several pieces are also unsafe: FAILED trades are never reversed, the REST poller ignores trade status, maker status updates attach to the wrong order id, keep-alive uses the wrong ping, there is no resync after reconnect and no heartbeat, and REST and on-chain calls block the tick loop. Carry over only the semantics listed under valuableKnowledge: the shared fill-id scheme, owner-filtered maker_orders, cancel-response handling, per-entry batch results, and once-per-trade fill emission.

On the user's broader question, from the execution side: porting block by block and aligning with V2 afterwards would be wasted work for live, since nothing there is worth aligning, but it is the right method for the backtest core, as long as ts-compat stays a thin config and is not a copy of the TS code. A second agent such as Fable fits well as an independent diff classifier. Give it the JSONL trace diffs plus the TS-bug / Rust-bug / intended-change list above, and have it propose a classification for each mismatch in PARITY.md. A human (or this session) should confirm each classification.

valuableKnowledge: Feed visibility clock is the row's local receive time, clamped up to the exchange time, and falls back to exchange time when local is missing or <=0, because the exchange stamp comes before the ~50-150ms delivery leg (wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:46-64; replayTelonexDeltaParquetForMarket.ts:174-180).

Binance: a trade at time T becomes visible when T+110ms <= clock (inclusive; 110 is the measured p50). The emitted point has tsMs=T and receivedAtMs=T+latency (backtestExternalFeedsProvider.ts:70-74,140-150; wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:28-37).
Binance same-ms ties go to the highest agg_trade_id, because the series is ordered by agg id and not by ts. That is live last-write-wins (binanceAggTradesSource.ts:5-14,83-86).

Chainlink two-clock model: visibility uses the BROADCAST time (server_timestamp_us) plus the bot leg, the emitted tsMs is the ROUND time, and receivedAtMs = broadcast+latency. The series is sorted by (broadcast, round), so the emitted round tsMs may legitimately step backwards (chainlinkCryptoPricesSource.ts:10-31,121-124; backtestExternalFeedsProvider.ts:99-109,152-162).

The 320ms chainlink latency was calibrated end-to-end by the parity harness. The raw network p50 of 235 left replay 86ms early. Do not 'correct' it to the raw latency, and never add the ~1s round-to-broadcast lag again (wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:71-87).

Price-to-beat becomes visible at window start + 2700ms (measured p50, max 5.4s), with receivedAtMs = availableAt, an uppercase slug symbol and ISO strings derived from the slug window. It is gone at market end, like live's clearPolymarketPriceToBeat on rotation (wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:102-110,290-298; backtestExternalFeedsProvider.ts:164-175; trading-bot.ts restartPriceToBeatIfNeeded).

Each series starts with the single latest value before the lookback range (binance by highest agg id, chainlink by broadcast order). Live's store keeps the last value forever, even across market rotations (binanceAggTradesSource.ts:20-25,77-95; chainlinkCryptoPricesSource.ts:110-136; externalFeeds.ts:113-158).

Lookback defaults to 300s. Series tails extend past endMs (binance 2s, chainlink 5s) because local clocks run past the exchange-stamped end. Day-file coverage excludes the end day at midnight, so fresh 23:45 markets do not hard-fail (binanceAggTradesSource.ts:32-43; chainlinkCryptoPricesSource.ts:33-44; binance/paths.ts:119-130).

All feed keys share one monotone high-water feed clock. This is load-bearing for telonex-delta: rows are sorted by exchange then local ts (parsing.ts:125-131), and combined price_change rows take the max local ts of the up/down pair (deltaTyped.ts:207-209,239), so local clocks go backwards (backtestExternalFeedsProvider.ts:63-68,136-139).

Snapshot shape follows the live store: rtdsPolymarketCryptoPrices:{} is always present even when empty, and binanceWsSpotPrice/chainlink/priceToBeat keys stay absent until first visible (externalFeeds.ts:129-136; backtestExternalFeedsProvider.ts:136).

Synthetic tie rule: flushing is STRICT (vis < real tick clock) but provider visibility is INCLUSIVE (vis <= clock). At equal times the real book tick already sees the new feed value, and the synthetic tick for that event fires after it (syntheticTickSchedule.ts:62-70,92; backtestExternalFeedsProvider.ts:73).

Synthetic schedule rules: bounded to the window inclusive on visibility; binance before chainlink on equal visibility; feed series order kept; events before the first real snapshot are consumed and never dispatched; the index only advances on backward clocks; flushTail runs after the stream (syntheticTickSchedule.ts:17-60,78-103; runSingleMarket.ts:346-378,492).
A synthetic tick is stamped max(visibility, last real snapshot ts) on an unchanged book, and its market key must equal the real ticks' key because plugin reset keys on it (syntheticTick.ts:21-72).

Synthetic ticks skip orderManager.onMarketTick, so no simulator fills, GTD expiry or latency-queue drain on a stale book. Plugins skip them unless they set handlesSyntheticTicks (StrategyRunner.ts:316-334; PluginSet.ts:72-78; ExternalFeedsRequestPlugin.ts:64-66).

Synthetic ticks are counted in eventsProcessed/eventsByType ('binance_agg_trade' / 'chainlink_round') before the window gate, so the dispatched count can be lower than the scheduled count and gated ticks are still counted (runSingleMarket.ts:297-315; adr-binance-driven-ticks.md:62-66).

Chainlink hard-error matrix: window start before 2026-04-02; missing day file, with a separate message when only today/yesterday UTC is missing (publication lag); zero rounds; NULL or <=0 broadcast ts; in-window round-clock gap >=300000ms, clipped to the window and bounded by seed and tail, disabled only by env=0 (chainlinkCryptoPricesSource.ts:69-104,146-170,193-249).

Binance hard errors: a missing day file (message names the worker R2-pull or producer download command) or zero trades. A seed-only series is just a warning, and there is no in-window gap check at replay (binanceAggTradesSource.ts:56-132).

Price-to-beat matrix: a backfilled strike is ALWAYS fed regardless of the series epoch. Null before the series epoch means the key stays absent. Producer didn't resolve means an internal error. Settled <30h ago means absent plus a warning. Catalog miss or never synced means an error naming the sync command. Synced but empty means an error for a Polymarket-side hole (wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:283-344).

Historical mode must reject chainlinkTwap, binanceBookTicker and chainlink-opening-twap priceToBeat rather than substitute another price (wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:176-181; ExternalFeedsRequestPlugin.ts:37-47).

Symbols: an explicit strategy symbol wins even when it doesn't match the slug (warn, same as live). Otherwise derive btc→btcusdt / btc/usd / btcusd. Book rules: `book` replaces the side (levels with size<=0 dropped), and price_change sets the new aggregate size (<=0 deletes). Telonex row decode skips rows with a blank market or null/negative ts_exchange_ms. asset_index refers to the row's asset0/asset1 columns (first-appearance order, not UP/DOWN). Bad side codes or unknown assets drop single changes, a row with no changes left is skipped, and every remaining row is one tick even if no level changed (replayTelonexDeltaParquetForMarket.ts:58-149,169-188; deltaTyped.ts:41-58).

audits.reasoning:
This subsystem is the most correct part of the TS engine. Its semantics are measured and calibrated against live data: the 110ms Binance latency, the 320ms Chainlink bot leg calibrated end-to-end by the parity harness, 2.7s for price-to-beat, the two-clock Chainlink model, seeding, tails and the hard-error policy. Unit tests pin them (backtestExternalFeedsProvider.test.ts, syntheticTickSchedule.test.ts, chainlinkCryptoPricesSource.test.ts). Most of what the user senses is missing (fees, FAK, taker delay, GTD, liquidity depletion, CLOB V2) lives in execution, not here.

The gaps that do belong here are structural:
- tick_size_change and last_trade_price are never exposed.
- Telonex-delta has no trade prints, so a queue-position fill model needs either the Telonex trades channel or Recorder V4.
- Feed latency knobs come from worker env and wall-clock rules, not the job.
- snapshot.timestamp mixes two clock domains.

So the behavior should be kept nearly verbatim, but the code shape should not. Not worth carrying over: float-keyed Maps, per-tick full-array snapshots, the env-driven depth cap, the dead binary-search branch, structuredClone per tick, the JS promise frame queue, and fill harvesting by diffing a capped list.

Recommended Rust shape:
- Fixed-point BTreeMap books (already in pmb-core market.rs).
- Ticks that carry both clocks explicitly.
- One merged discrete-event timeline: market rows on the feed clock plus feed visibility events.
- Explicit tie rules matching TS: feed state is visible inclusively, while synthetic dispatch is strictly after the real tick; binance before chainlink; drop until first book; monotone high-water clock.
- All knobs and `now` passed in MarketJobData.

That same scheduler later takes Recorder V4 recorded receive times with no new semantics. The TS replay must serve as the oracle: emit per-tick traces (cause, exchange ts, local ts, feed values visible) from the existing src/backtest/parity/trace.ts and diff them on ~200 telonex-delta markets, both opted-in and not opted-in to synthetic ticks.

Rust WIP state: telonex.rs and feeds/binance.rs look faithful and tested. The crate does not compile because lib.rs and feeds/mod.rs declare modules that were never written: input, chainlink, price_to_beat, schedule, state. Finishing them against the TS oracle is cheaper than a clean rewrite, and is low-risk if the trace diff is the acceptance gate.

audits.reasoning:
The backtest coupling is a narrow, JSON-only seam. MarketJobData goes in and RunSingleMarketOutput comes out. Of the result, consumers persist and read about 17 MarketStats fields plus skipReason/coverageReasons and execution meta, and no per-fill data is persisted anywhere (backtest_run_markets has no trades table). No consumer therefore forces a block-by-block port of the TypeScript internals (OrderManager, Portfolio, BacktestExecution). A clean Rust core built for the realistic model (fixed-point, event stream, per-market ExchangeRules, seeded latency, fee on the fill, CLOB V2 later) can sit behind the seam, as long as it keeps a few semantics exactly: skip and denominator rules, 2 dp per-market rounding feeding batch sums, the window gate that stops the simulator and plugins, eventsProcessed counting, and intentMeta ordering. The TS engine should act as an oracle, not a template: the ts-compat profile is a set of config flags on the same core, checked against TS through the parity trace on unrounded values. TS has to stay anyway, because 75 TS strategies, external #pmb artifacts, the Recorder V4 reuse of src/market and the feed clients, and the live bot all depend on it.

The wide couplings are elsewhere: the in-process simulator observer, the live WebUI getState and commands, the user-WS account sources, and ExternalFeedsRequestConfig shared across eligibility, the DB and the dashboard. Rust must expose one TraceSink event stream (converted in TS into both the simulator chunks and the parity JSONL) and a live snapshot/command API with the same JSON shapes. The job contract needs additive fields: an explicit engineConfig replacing the worker env knobs, a latency seed, producer-resolved exchangeRules, and an engine/profile identity column on backtest_runs. The TS wrapper, not Rust, should stamp execution meta and recorderV4Capture; today's native path loses machineId (marketProcessor.ts:58), and the simulator cannot replay native runs (resolveMarket.ts:106).

valuableKnowledge: fixed.rs:11-134 — Price/Qty/Usdc newtypes in 1e-6 micros with i128 intermediates and explicit Round modes; div_round Nearest rounds half toward +inf, which matches JS Math.round for negative PnL (stats test pnl_rounds_half_up_like_math_round). Keep as is.

rules.rs:85-103 — exact integer fee curve size*rate*(p(1-p))^e, rounded half-up to dp, where a fee that rounds to zero is the 'min fee' rule; tests rules.rs:286-334 include the TS capital vector (800 @ 0.6 -> 493.44 reservation). Reusable math.

rules.rs:129-240 — realistic constants worth carrying over: no crypto taker fee before 2026-01-05 (1_767_571_200_000), 0.07 rate from 2026-03-30, GTD lead 180 s and early expiry 60 s, batch cap 15, valid price range [tick, 1-tick].

market.rs:238-335 — order-book semantics: a snapshot replaces the book and drops size<=0 levels (last duplicate wins); price_change sets the aggregate size (0 removes); deltas before the first book are applied but flagged; unknown assets are ignored; last_trade_price never changes levels. Tests at market.rs:499-624. Directly reusable.

telonex.rs:1-10,243-311 — delta-typed row rules: skip a row on blank market, null/negative ts_exchange, unknown event type or unresolvable asset index. asset_index refers to the row's own asset0/asset1 columns (file order), NOT UP/DOWN. A market mismatch is a hard error. Easy to get wrong in a rewrite.
telonex.rs:44-50 — feed visibility clock for a real tick = max(ts_local, ts_exchange), falling back to exchange time when local is missing or <=0 (TS feedClockMs).

pq.rs:36-121,140-177 — column-wise Parquet reader with def/rep levels mapped to per-row value ranges, buffer reuse across row groups, and row-group pruning by min/max stats including 'seed-only' groups. Fast and reusable for any as-of series.

binance.rs:4-10,99-163 — aggTrade series is ordered by agg_trade_id (same-ms ties resolve to the highest id = live last-write-wins), seeded with the single latest pre-window trade, extended by a 2 s tail. A missing day file or no trade before window end is a hard error; seed groups are pruned by max id.

feeds/mod.rs:46-88 — measured feed defaults (Binance 110 ms, Chainlink broadcast->bot 320 ms, PTB 2700 ms, 300 s lookbacks, 300 s Chainlink max gap) and env override rules (empty, negative or non-integer keeps the default).

portfolio.rs:151-172,725-771 — capital rule: a BUY reserves notional + taker fee unless post-only, and the reservation is released only by an authoritative final quantity (reject, kill, fill, or done with filled_size); a done event without filled_size keeps the hold. Correct conservative model to keep.

portfolio.rs:884-1153 — tests ported from the TS capital suite (late ack, fill before ack, client-id reuse generations, filled-status-before-fills). Good regression vectors for a future live reconciliation layer even if Portfolio is redesigned.

audits.reasoning:
The WIP is about 7.9k lines of Rust, roughly 1.3k of them tests. It is idiomatic at the surface: no unsafe, fixed-point newtypes, serde-tagged enums, BTreeMap for determinism, traits for Execution/TraceSink/CandleSource, and a zero-copy Parquet reader. Architecturally, though, it is a module-by-module transliteration of the TS engine. order_manager.rs mirrors OrderManager.ts + riskLimits.ts down to check order and reason strings. portfolio.rs carries over Portfolio.ts + capital.ts, including two parallel ledgers and the live-WS identity reconciliation. stats.rs copies the TS PnL decomposition, and plugin snapshots copy TS JSON shapes. It also inherits TS's async-queue bookkeeping (unapplied submissions, pending capital), which a deterministic single-threaded Rust loop does not need.

The quirk flags are a good idea, but they are incomplete and partly wrong. TS's per-fill round2 accounting is not modeled, so ts-compat will not hit the 1e-6 parity target. The TS-shaped stats formula double-counts split cost once the realistic profile gives split shares a cost basis. TS also drops merge proceeds from PnL (a TS bug that ts-compat faithfully reproduces).

The decisive point: the engine's real value (fill simulator, queue/depletion, seeded latency, scheduler, runner/cascade, strategy SDK, binary) does not exist yet. The tree does not compile: two module declarations are missing in pmb-core, and five module files are missing in pmb-replay. OrderManager has no tests at all. So a clean-slate core loses almost nothing.

Recommendation:
- Do not keep the stateful core (order_manager, portfolio/capital, stats PnL formula, the plugin framework shape) as a base. Redesign it from first principles: a single ordered event loop that applies events to one ledger as they are emitted, outcome-indexed assets, engine-assigned order ids, live reconciliation moved into the live adapter, and PnL computed from cash.
- Do salvage the leaf modules by copying them into the new design: fixed.rs, market.rs book semantics, the rules.rs fee curve, pq.rs, the telonex.rs reader, the binance.rs loader, slug.rs, the TA/volatility math, and the Execution/TraceSink seam.
- Salvage the oracle infrastructure too: golden generators that run the real TS code, TRACE.md plus the TS trace writer and diff, and the engine exerciser.

Use TS as an oracle only for business behaviors that matter (book semantics, feed visibility clocks, indicator math, fee curve, capital reservation). Every TS accounting quirk, such as round2, merge PnL and the zero-basis split, gets classified in PARITY.md instead of being reproduced by default.

judgments.summary: Go with C, the hybrid. Viewed through correctness confidence, the engine has to answer three separate questions, and each needs its own evidence. First, are the mechanics right: cascade order, capital reservation, dedupe and generations, feed visibility clocks, book semantics, the stats contract? The TS engine is a good oracle there, and its ~4.9k lines of tests hold behavior that took a long time to get right. Option B throws that away, which makes it the weakest choice for mechanics. Second, is execution realistic? TS is known to be wrong here (worst-queue full fills, no depletion, a free fill on the crossing remainder, fixed 700 bps), so matching TS proves nothing. Only live fills compared against a V4 replay of the same market can prove it, and option A's ts-compat profile can only prove the port. Third, is the live adapter right? There is no oracle: TS live has been broken since the V2 cutover. Here the evidence is the spec, recorded WS fixtures, a dry run, and tiny real orders. To make the TS oracle work end-to-end, I would keep a thin TsCompat implementation of the FillModel, LatencyModel and FeeModel traits. Without it, the first diverging fill cascades and the trace diff becomes useless.
howToExecute: 1. Triage the WIP (about half a day). Make it compile by declaring order_manager and rules in pmb-core lib.rs, and by stubbing or deleting the missing pmb-replay modules input, chainlink, price_to_beat, schedule and state. Keep the leaf modules: fixed.rs, market.rs book semantics, pq.rs, telonex.rs, feeds/binance.rs, slug.rs, the TA/volatility math, the rules.rs fee curve, and the Execution/TraceSink traits. Drop order_manager.rs, the CashBook and pending machinery in portfolio.rs, and the PnL formula in stats.rs as foundations. Keep their test vectors as fixtures.

2. Write native/SPEC.md as the single design source. It has three parts: (a) current Polymarket rules, citing the docs pages: per-market feeSchedule with 5 dp rounding and no crypto fee before 2026-01-05; taker delay dated by trade time (250 ms, then 50 ms from 2026-08-17, then 150 ms from 2026-09-04); GTD at least 3 min out with effective expiry 60 s early; tick and minimum size; batch of at most 15; FOK/FAK semantics, with market BUYs sized in USDC; V2 order struct and EIP-712 domain version 2; the user-WS message mapping. (b) The output contract: RunSingleMarketOutput, MarketStats field rules, skip and denominator rules, the eventsProcessed and window-gate rules, intentMeta ordering. (c) The list of TS behaviors to keep, taken from the six audits.

3. Get independent tests. A second agent (Fable, or a separate session) writes conformance tests from SPEC.md only, without seeing the implementation. The implementing agent never writes the spec tests. This removes correlated misreadings, the most common failure when one agent writes both the code and its tests.

4. Build the core cleanly. It is a single-threaded discrete-event loop with one ledger that applies events as they are emitted, so no unapplied-submission overlay is needed. It uses engine-assigned submission generation ids, outcome-indexed assets, and an explicit two-clock tick (exchange time plus visibility time). PnL is computed from cash (cash_end − start + settlement value), and debug builds assert that it equals the cost-basis decomposition. FillModel, LatencyModel and FeeModel are traits. Seeds, `now` and every worker-env knob (feed latencies, max gap, depth levels, drain budget) move into MarketJobData.engineConfig.

5. Add a TsCompat implementation for each of the three traits, about 200-300 lines in total: worst-queue full fill, no depletion, a free maker fill on the crossing remainder, actions applied on the next real tick, jitter 0, 700 bps at 4 dp, MATCHED on accept. These are model implementations, not a port. Accounting quirks that do not change decisions are NOT reproduced: the merge-PnL loss, cash/PnL divergence on oversells, split basis. They are listed in PARITY.md as TS bugs.

6. Gate the mechanics with the oracle. Convert the TS unit suites into Rust fixture tests: capital.test, cancellation.test, Portfolio.test, restPollCapital.test, StrategyRunner.{serial,clock,syntheticTicks}.test, runnerConfig.test, the syntheticTickSchedule and feed-provider tests, plus the existing stats_gen and plugins_gen goldens. Add proptest invariants: cash conservation, reservations that are never negative and are released only on an authoritative final quantity, no oversell in realistic, and byte-identical output for the same job and seed, including inside run-group. Then run the trace diff on about 200 telonex-delta markets with the extended exerciser and lagsnipe.v15, both opted-in and not opted-in to synthetic ticks. Before diffing, extend the exerciser with: same-cid cancel-then-replace in one list, a repeat place of an active cid, intents from an order_submitted callback, the 101-order cap, a funding reject, merge twice in one list, and cancel_batch on an in-flight order under latency. Compare cash-based PnL on both sides: the TS simulator trace already computes it (simulator/contracts.ts:180), which sidesteps the TS merge bug without copying it.

7. Build the realistic profile from SPEC.md: queue-ahead taken from the recorded size at our price on arrival, depletion by our own orders, separate seeded place and cancel latency at exact event time, the taker delay, and validation. Each fix gets an A/B report against TsCompat on the same 200 markets.

8. Run the live identity proof (M7). The Rust live runtime journals its inputs with its own receive times in a replayable format. Replaying a dry-run journal through the backtest path must give an identical decision sequence. This proves that live and backtest run the same deterministic code, something TS never proved.

9. Build the live V2 adapter (M8) in parallel once the core and the Execution trait exist. Test it against the docs' signing vectors and recorded user-WS and REST fixtures. Cover: FAILED/RETRYING trades are reversed, maker status attaches to our maker order id, a text PING every 10 s, resync after reconnect, POST /heartbeats every 5 s, non-blocking placement, and terminal events derived from the REST insert status.

10. Calibrate with ~$100. This needs an explicit user decision, because GOAL.md has real-money activation out of scope; see calibrationWith100Usd. Feed the results back into the realistic-profile parameters, and report realistic-vs-live error on held-out days.
11. Integrate the fleet and benchmark (M5/M6) only after steps 6-8 pass. The TS wrapper, not Rust, stamps execution meta and recorderV4Capture.
judgments.howCorrectnessIsProven:
The proof is layered. Each layer proves a different claim, and no single layer is enough.

1. Spec conformance. An independent agent writes tests from SPEC.md and the Polymarket docs, covering fees, taker delay, GTD, tick/min size, FOK/FAK, batch cap, V2 signing vectors, and user-WS mapping. This proves the rules are implemented as published.

2. Property and invariant tests. Cash-based PnL must equal the cost-basis decomposition. Cash is conserved. Reservations never go negative. Realistic mode never oversells. The same job and seed give byte-identical output, including in run-group and in a different order. This proves internal consistency and determinism. It would have caught the TS merge-PnL bug (confirmed: Portfolio.ts:562 credits cash, no PnL is realized, and marketStats.ts:163 never sees the merge) and the WIP's double-counted split cost (confirmed: portfolio.rs adds the split basis, and stats.rs subtracts split_cost again).

3. TS differential on mechanics. Converted TS unit suites, plus an end-to-end trace diff on ~200 telonex-delta markets under the TsCompat models. The order, fill and cancel sequence must be identical. Sizes, USDC and cash-based PnL must match within 1e-6. Every mismatch is classified in PARITY.md. A note for the classifier: TS round2 is really 8 dp (rounding.ts:10-12). The audit claim that Rust micros drift 0.005 per fill is wrong; the real per-operation residue is at most 5e-7. Rare decision flips from that residue get classified, not emulated.

4. Live/backtest identity. A dry-run journal replayed through the backtest path must give identical decisions (M7). This proves one deterministic core.

5. Execution ground truth. Real micro-orders, with the same markets recorded by Recorder V4, replayed with the live decisions injected at their actual send times. Compare, per order: filled or not, fill time, partial size, price, maker or taker, exact fee, and the taker-delay outcome. Report Brier score for maker fill probability, time-to-fill error, and the fee match rate on held-out days. This is the only layer that proves backtest execution is close to live.
biggestRisks: Execution ground truth is blocked on live. TS live is CLOB V1 and broken. Calibration needs the Rust V2 adapter, plus a user decision to activate real money, which GOAL.md lists as out of scope. Until then, the realistic profile is validated only against the spec, not against reality.

ts-compat can creep into a port. If TsCompat grows beyond the three model traits into copied OrderManager/Portfolio structure (the WIP already did this), the project turns back into option A and drifts toward emulating JS. Cap it at trait implementations, and classify accounting quirks instead of reproducing them.

Correlated errors. If the same agent writes the implementation, the spec tests and the parity classifications, a misread doc becomes a passing test. Spec tests and diff classification need independent authorship (Fable or a separate session), and the user must confirm any classification that changes money semantics.

Small calibration sample. ~$100 at minimum order sizes gives a few hundred orders, which is not enough to fit a full queue model. Live data should validate and tune a few parameters (one-way place/cancel latency, a queue-ahead multiplier, fee exactness). The model's structure should come from V4 trade prints. Check results on held-out days to avoid overfitting.

Telonex-delta has no trade prints. The realistic queue model is weaker there, because cancels and trades at our level look the same. Quantify the gap by comparing realistic-on-telonex against realistic-on-V4 for overlapping BTC 15m markets before trusting telonex realistic results.

Clock mismatch in calibration. worker-2's V4 receive times differ from the live machine's receive times. The live bot must journal its own receive times, and the comparison must align on exchange timestamps, not on V4 receipt order.

Nondeterminism in the oracle itself: unseeded jitter, worker-env feed knobs, and wall-clock rules (the 30h price-to-beat grace, the publication-lag branch). Unless these are pinned, the TS reference traces are not reproducible, and diffs become noise.

Long-term dual-engine drift. 75 TS strategies stay on the TS engine with the old execution model. Results from the two engines are not comparable unless every run row records its engine and profile identity.
judgments.calibrationWith100Usd:
This is the only source of truth for execution, so treat it as its own measurement track, not as a final smoke test. It also needs a user decision first.

Prerequisites:
- A working V2 live path. The Rust adapter (M8) is preferred; patching TS to clob-client-v2 is a stopgap only if calendar time matters more than tokens.
- The user, not the agent, activates signing and launches the bot, in line with GOAL rule 8 and this machine's DRY_RUN=false hazard.
- Markets are BTC 5m/15m only, because worker-2's Recorder V4 records only those, including last trades.

Design:
- A scripted probe strategy, an exerciser-like schedule and not alpha: post-only orders at the touch, orders inside the spread, behind-touch GTC orders, FAK/FOK takers, and cancels at fixed offsets. Use minimum sizes (about 5 shares, ~$2-5 per order).
- Capital recycles as markets resolve, so $100 supports a few hundred orders over several days.
- Journal everything raw: REST request and response timestamps and insert status, every user-WS frame with local receive time, and an end-of-day reconciliation against the CLOB trades history. Calibrate from these raw exchange records, never from the bot's own accounting.

Analysis:
- Replay each recorded V4 market with the live decisions injected at their actual send times, under the realistic profile.
- Compare per order: filled or not, fill time, partial size, price, maker or taker, exact fee, and taker-delay behavior.
- Fit separate one-way place and cancel latency distributions from ack timestamps versus match times.
- Validate the per-market feeSchedule formula against the fees actually charged; this should be an exact match.
- Tune only a few parameters (the latency distributions and a queue-ahead multiplier), and report the error on held-out days.

Results go into the realistic profile defaults. The A/B reports should then show realistic-vs-live error next to realistic-vs-TsCompat.

judgments.summary: Go with C. Polymarket's current docs plus the MarketStats/RunSingleMarketOutput contract define the engine. The TS engine is used only as a test oracle, and only where it is correct: replay, book, feed visibility, plugin math, runner event ordering and capital reservation. A block-by-block port wastes compute in the two places where most of the missing features are. Live has had no working oracle since the CLOB V2 cutover on 2026-04-28. Execution would have to be rebuilt anyway for fees, FAK, the taker delay, GTD, depletion and queue position. The Rust WIP confirms the risk: order_manager.rs and portfolio.rs are transliterations of the TS async architecture, not a design, while the leaf modules (fixed-point types, book, Parquet/telonex/binance readers, fee math, plugin math) are solid and should be kept. Keep 'ts-compat', but shrink it to a few fill-model flags that line up trades for a trace diff. TS accounting quirks get classified in PARITY.md, not reproduced. Live micro-trading on top of Recorder V4 recordings becomes the only ground truth for execution realism, and data collection should start early, in parallel, with a small probe the user runs.

8. In parallel from step 1, run a calibration probe. It is a small standalone script on the official V2 client, run by the user with a hard budget cap, a kill switch and a heartbeat. It is never the TS trading-bot.

judgments.roleOfTsEngine:
The TS engine stays frozen and in production for unported strategies, orchestration and Recorder V4, which reuses src/market and the feed clients. It is not a design template. It is a test oracle in four areas:
1. Replay, order book and feed visibility: near-verbatim semantics, checked by per-tick trace diff.
2. Plugin math, through the existing golden generators.
3. Strategy-observable runner ordering: FIFO cascades, rejections before executions, the tick-scoped plugin snapshot, nowMs as an event clock.
4. Capital reservation rules: cash released only on an authoritative final quantity; per-market allowance isolation.

For execution, TS supplies only a thin compat fill model, so traces line up long enough to prove the rest of the port. Its accounting quirks are classified, not reproduced:
- Merge proceeds are lost from MarketStats.pnl. I checked this: Portfolio.ts:562 credits cash, the cost basis is kept, and marketStats.ts never sees the merge.
- Oversells are credited to cash but only partly to PnL.

One audit claim is wrong: per-fill round2 drift is not a parity problem. round2 rounds to 8 dp (rounding.ts:10-12), which is below the 1e-6 tolerance. The 4 dp per-fill fee rounding does matter, and it lives in the compat fee model.

TS is not an oracle for live behavior (live has been broken since V2), for exchange rules (use the docs), or for fill realism (use live data). No realistic fixes are backported to TS.
judgments.howCorrectnessIsProven:
There are five layers, each a CI or report gate.

1. Leaf goldens. Rust is checked against output from the real TS code for book semantics, telonex decode, feed visibility, plugin math and the fee curve. Exchange rules are table tests, each citing the Polymarket doc it comes from.

2. Invariants and property tests:
- Determinism: same job and seed give byte-identical output.
- PnL: cash_end - start + settlement value equals the cost-basis decomposition.
- Reservations are always released.
- In realistic: no negative inventory, and liquidity is conserved under depletion.

3. Trace parity against TS, with the compat fill model and jitter 0. Cases: the extended engine-exerciser plus lagsnipe.v15 on about 200 telonex-delta markets. Requirements:
- the order/fill/cancel sequence, sides and prices are identical;
- unrounded USDC and PnL match within 1e-6;
- every mismatch is classified in PARITY.md (TS bug, Rust bug, or intended change), with a scratch reproduction for each TS bug.

4. A/B reports for every realistic fix on the same markets.

5. Ground truth from live:
- The M7 journal replay through the backtest path gives identical decisions.
- The calibration probe journals are compared with Rust replays of the same intents on the worker-2 V4 recordings. Metrics: maker fill or no-fill, time to fill, fill size, taker slippage, fee, and the place/cancel/taker-delay latency distributions, each reported with confidence intervals.
biggestRisks: Clean-slate drift in behavior strategies can observe (cascade order, plugin snapshot timing, the nowMs clock, rejection ordering). Ported strategies would then decide differently from their TS backtests. Mitigation: trace parity on the order sequence under the compat fill model before any realistic change.

Budget burn from chasing a bit-perfect ts-compat: TS accounting quirks, async bookkeeping and the 500-entry recentFills harvest. Mitigation: compat covers the fill model only, everything else is classified, and each milestone is time-boxed per rule 6.

Not enough ground truth for the queue and partial-fill model. Telonex-delta has no trade prints, and about $100 buys only a few hundred tiny orders, enough for latency and fee checks but too few to fit a queue model, which would then be overfit. Mitigation: report confidence intervals, validate depletion statistically on V4 trade prints across many markets, and keep worst-queue available as the conservative bound.

Our own orders contaminate the calibration recordings. worker-2's V4 book includes our resting orders, unlike historical data. Our size must be subtracted from recorded levels and queue-ahead during calibration replays, or results will be biased.

Per-market metadata is missing: feeSchedule, secondsDelay, tick size and min size are not stored anywhere, and historical values may not be recoverable from Gamma for old markets. The realistic profile then falls back to a dated table, and the Jan-Mar 2026 fee row comes from third-party reports.

Real-money safety in the V2 live adapter: signing, heartbeat dead-man switch, FAILED-trade reversal, reconnect resync, and this machine's DRY_RUN=false env. Mitigation: dry-run first, probe fixtures as tests, and the user activates in a separate session. The agent never places orders.
Two engines in production produce results that are not comparable. Mitigation: an engine/profile/engineVersion column on backtest_runs, with engineConfig persisted in the job instead of worker env.
Rate-limit interruptions leave half-done, non-compiling WIP again (this happened at fef5f199). Mitigation: small steps that each compile and are committed, with STATUS.md updated at each one.

Do not transliterate: the TS execution layer is wrong in ways you must not copy (full-size worst-queue fills, no depletion, free remainder fill, hardcoded 700 bps, unseeded jitter, merge proceeds lost from PnL), and the previous Codex attempt shows a 1e-6 money-parity target pulls the port into JS emulation. judgments.roleOfTsEngine: Four roles, none of them 'design template'. (1) Test oracle on the believed-correct subset, via traces and generated golden fixtures: order-book semantics, Telonex row decode rules, feed visibility clocks (110/320/2700 ms, two-clock Chainlink, seeding/tails, hard-error matrix), synthetic-tick tie rules, plugin math, fee curve, capital-reservation rules (release only on authoritative final quantity, trade-status sizes not cumulative, cid reuse guard, fill-before-ack buffering), breadth-first cascade order, per-market allowance isolation, and the parity trace sequence from engine-exerciser and lagsnipe.v15 under ts-compat. Its 93 node:test files become data vectors for Rust tests, not code to port. (2) Explicit non-oracle for execution realism, accounting shape and live: the simulator's fill model, the merge-PnL and oversell bugs, the pending-capital overlay, object-identity maps and the V1-signed, status-ignoring live adapter are classified in PARITY.md, never reproduced outside ts-compat flags. (3) Production engine that stays untouched for the ~60 unported strategies, external artifacts, research protocols, and as the dependency of Recorder V4 (src/market, feed clients). (4) Orchestration owner: producer, BullMQ fleet, aggregation/segments, MySQL, dashboard, WebUI; the TS wrapper stamps execution meta and converts the Rust TraceSink stream into both the simulator chunks and the parity JSONL.
judgments.howCorrectnessIsProven: Layered, each layer independent of the next. (1) Leaf semantics: Rust unit tests against golden JSON generated by running the real TS code (existing stats_gen/plugins_gen pattern extended to book, feed visibility, synthetic schedule, fee rounding). (2) Ordering and capital: capital.test.ts, cancellation.test.ts, StrategyRunner.*.test.ts and runnerConfig.test.ts replayed as event-sequence fixtures with expected snapshots. (3) Engine parity: TRACE.md JSONL diff on ~200 telonex-delta markets with the extended engine-exerciser and lagsnipe.v15 in ts-compat — event sequence, sides, prices, sizes exact; USDC/PnL within 1e-4 and final stats at 2 dp; every mismatch classified in PARITY.md as TS bug / Rust bug / intended change, with a classifier model proposing and a human confirming. (4) Invariants compiled into the core as debug assertions: cash + reserved + inventory identities, pnl_from_cash == decomposition, fee == schedule(fill), no negative inventory in realistic, monotone engine clock, deterministic re-run byte-identical given the seed. (5) Output contract: schema tests for RunSingleMarketOutput and MarketStats (skip semantics, eventsByType keys, intentMeta order) against TS fixtures, and a fleet run whose aggregation and dashboard render unchanged. (6) Realistic profile: A/B report per fix on identical markets, plus tape-based fill-model evaluation on Recorder V4 captures with trade prints. (7) Live: dry-run journal replayed through the backtest path must reproduce identical decisions; then $100 micro-trading compared order-by-order against Recorder V4 capture of the same markets (fill yes/no, time, size, fee, latency), summarized in PARITY-LIVE.md.
biggestRisks: Token/session budget: the parts that do not exist yet (event loop, simulator, scheduler, SDK, replay modules, binary, live runtime, V2 adapter) are the bulk of the work, and the WIP shows agents hitting limits mid-module. Mitigate with leaf-first order, compile-green commits per step, and strict time boxes per GOAL.md rule 6.

Parity-target drift: a 1e-6 money target forces per-fill float emulation (round2 at 8 dp, 4 dp fee rounding, 2 dp qty) — the exact failure mode of the abandoned Codex branch. Mitigate by relaxing rule 4 to sequence-exact plus classified money residuals before parity work starts.

Live has no oracle: TS live is V1-signed and broken, and its user-WS handling is unsafe (FAILED never reversed, maker status attached to taker id, wrong keep-alive, no heartbeat, no resync). The V2 adapter must be designed from docs and verified first in dry-run and then with the $100 budget; it adds a non-trivial, unplanned-as-mandatory milestone.

Missing per-market exchange metadata: no feeSchedule, secondsDelay, tick size or min size is stored anywhere, so the realistic profile has no data source until the TS catalog captures Gamma fields and the producer passes exchangeRules in the job.

Fill-model realism is only partially testable: telonex-delta has no trade prints, the recorded book never contains our orders, and $100 yields tens of fills — enough for latency and rule validation, not for fine queue statistics. Combine with V4 tape evaluation and the Telonex trades follow-up.

Two engines diverge: ~60 TS strategies and research protocols keep running on the TS engine with its known biases while Rust-backed results use realistic; batch comparisons across engines will mislead unless runs carry an engine/profile identity column.

Ops seams already leak: the native worker path drops machineId/worker identity, the market simulator cannot replay native runs, queue jobs are SHA-gated, and lagsnipe.v15 lives in an external repo — each is small but blocks the fleet milestone if discovered late.

Real-money safety: this machine's env files force DRY_RUN=false; the agent must never launch any bot, and the first live Rust run needs heartbeat, kill switch and a tiny budget regardless of how good the tests look.

judgments.calibrationWith100Usd: It is the only ground truth for execution realism, but it comes late and is user-operated: it requires the Rust CLOB V2 adapter (TS live cannot place orders since 2026-04-28), and the user launches the bot while the agent never does (GOAL rule 8; this machine's env forces DRY_RUN=false). Design: a 'micro-probe' strategy variant (not the exerciser, whose 200-share crossing order would exceed the budget) that over ~20-30 BTC 15m windows places 5-share orders of every kind — resting maker BUYs at the touch and one/two ticks behind on both outcomes, small FOK/FAK takers, GTD, post-only that should reject, cancel-and-replace — with a per-window loss cap. The Rust live runtime journals every intent, REST response status, user-WS message and feed value with receive timestamps; worker-2's Recorder V4 records the same markets with books and trade prints. Afterwards: replay the journaled intents through the backtest path on the V4 capture under the realistic profile and compare per order — filled or not, fill time, fill size, fee, taker delay observed, MATCHED→MINED timing, any FAILED trades; fit separate place and cancel latency distributions from intent to ack and to portfolio visibility; verify the feeSchedule and GTD rules against real fills. Expectation: tens of fills is enough to validate rules, latency and gross fill-model errors and to prove the V2 adapter end to end; it is not enough to fit queue-position statistics, which come from the V4 tape evaluation over hundreds of markets. Output is PARITY-LIVE.md plus fitted model parameters checked into the realistic profile; only after that does the user decide to make realistic the default or raise capital.
